title: release-gate-probe negative control is stale (0.14.1 accepts [targets]) and its Windows extract fails on a D:\ tar path
description: Measured on release.yml publish=false dispatches 39826035054 (#646 head a021f560) and 39831687843 (dev 2769973e, the control): both reproduce the same two reds in all six release gate probe jobs, so neither comes from LCLI-750. (1) linux/darwin: the previous release (npm latest 0.14.1) now accepts [targets], so `--expect absent` exits 0 where the probe requires `Unrecognized key: "targets"`; the negative control must be re-based on a release that actually rejects the feature, or on another feature. (2) win32: GNU tar in Git bash reads `D:\a\_temp\...` as host:path ("tar: D\:\a\\_temp/lore-release-gate-probe-fresh-win32-x64: Cannot open", exit 2), so the Windows legs never reach the probe; the extract must use a path tar accepts (relative, or --force-local). Floor work: scripts/release-gate-probe.mjs and release.yml, needs a reviewer pass. setup-quest itself is fine on win32 (installed 0.14.1 from npm and asserted it).
implementationNotes: Scope narrowed pending an opum-doc ruling: this PR fixes only the win32 extract (tar -C with D:\ RUNNER_TEMP read as host:path); the stale-control half cannot be built because git diff v0.14.1..HEAD -- src .lore is empty, so no feature exists that the fresh binary accepts and 0.14.1 rejects. Reported to team-lead.
